evidence.snippet: trio whole exome sequencing did not establish an alternative secondary genetic diagnosis for autism, and reported long-term follow-up of IBDD patients is limited, it is possible that autism spectrum disorders could be one of the disease-associated features.
evidence.explanation: Single-case evidence supports only a tentative downstream association.

edges/10.description: Autism has been reported in a single IBDD case without an alternative genetic diagnosis, but causality remains uncertain.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals are either asymptomatic or display a variety of symptoms during infancy, including speech delay, cognitive impairment, failure to thrive, hypotonia, and emesis.
evidence.explanation: Review text lists emesis among reported IBDD symptoms.

edges/11.description: Emesis is reported among nonspecific symptomatic presentations.

evidence.snippet: one patient required frequent hospitalizations due to emesis and dehydration but is developing normally at 5 years of age.
evidence.explanation: Follow-up cohort reports dehydration in one symptomatic IBDD patient.

edges/12.description: Recurrent dehydration requiring hospitalization has been reported in one symptomatic patient.

evidence.snippet: Though we suspect IBDD did not contribute to hypoglycaemia in this patient, patients should be followed-up carefully
evidence.explanation: Authors explicitly caution that causality for hypoglycemia is uncertain.

edges/13.description: Ketotic hypoglycemia has been reported, but the authors considered causality uncertain.

evidence.snippet: All patients presented continuously elevated C4-acylcarnitine levels with higher ratios of C4/C2 and C4/C3. Isobutyrylglycine occurred in only 8 patients.
evidence.explanation: Patient cohort data directly connect the ACAD8 valine-catabolism defect to the characteristic C4-acylcarnitine and isobutyrylglycine biomarker pattern.

edges/14.description: ACAD8 loss blocks valine catabolism and diverts accumulating isobutyryl-CoA into detectable C4 and glycine conjugates.

evidence.snippet: Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is a defect in valine metabolism and was first reported in a child with cardiomyopathy, anemia, and secondary carnitine deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The index case supports decreased circulating carnitine as a rare downstream biochemical phenotype.

edges/15.description: Accumulated isobutyryl-CoA can be conjugated to carnitine, causing secondary depletion of circulating carnitine in rare symptomatic cases.

evidence.snippet: altered biochemical markers of liver function were reported in 19 individuals
evidence.explanation: Human literature synthesis supports liver biochemical abnormalities in a subset of IBDD individuals.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous mutant mice hepatocytes had abnormal mitochondria with crystalline inclusions, suggestive of mitochondriopathy.
evidence.explanation: ACAD8-deficient mouse data provide model-organism support for hepatic mitochondrial involvement.

edges/16.description: Reported liver-test abnormalities and the ACAD8-deficient mouse liver phenotype suggest a possible hepatic consequence, but the intervening mechanism remains unresolved.

evidence.snippet: SBCAD was not the sole ACAD responsible for this compensation, which indicates substantial promiscuity of ACADs in HEK-293 cells for the isobutyryl-CoA substrate.
evidence.explanation: In vitro ACAD substrate promiscuity supports a plausible compensatory mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Of these 172 individuals, 146 were asymptomatic at follow-up, whereas 26 presented with diverse, non-specific manifestations
evidence.explanation: Human literature synthesis supports the downstream low-penetrance clinical pattern.

edges/17.description: ACAD substrate promiscuity may help explain why most reported ACAD8-deficient individuals remain clinically asymptomatic despite persistent biochemical abnormalities.

evidence.snippet: One 11-year-old boy exhibited hepatomegaly and ultrasound findings suggestive of hepatic steatosis, along with markedly elevated transaminase levels.
evidence.explanation: Literature synthesis reports a human case with imaging findings suggestive of hepatic steatosis.

evidence.snippet: The mutant mice grew normally but demonstrated cold intolerance at young age with a progressive hepatic steatosis.
evidence.explanation: ACAD8-deficient mouse data support hepatic steatosis as a model-organism finding.

edges/18.description: One reported human case and the ACAD8-deficient mouse model suggest possible hepatic steatosis, although causality remains uncertain.

evidence.snippet: Both the genotypes and ACAD8 variants in IBDD are highly heterogeneous, and no significant correlations between genotype and phenotype are present here in patients with IBDD.
evidence.explanation: Confirms high genetic heterogeneity and absence of genotype-phenotype correlation.

evidence.snippet: Statistical analysis of these parameters did not establish significant differences amongst both groups.
evidence.explanation: No significant genotype-phenotype correlation found when comparing symptomatic and asymptomatic groups.

evidence.snippet: ACAD8 | HGNC:87 | isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency | MONDO:0012648 | AR | Definitive
evidence.explanation: ClinGen classifies the ACAD8-isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency gene-disease relationship as definitive with autosomal recessive inheritance.

evidence.snippet: All patients were regularly monitored once they were diagnosed, and each patient gradually had a normal diet after 6 months of age.
evidence.explanation: Describes conservative monitoring approach with gradual diet normalization.

evidence.snippet: Though we suspect IBDD did not contribute to hypoglycaemia in this patient, patients should be followed-up carefully
evidence.explanation: Supports careful monitoring due to uncertain clinical significance.

treatments/0.description: Given the uncertain clinical significance of IBDD, most patients identified through newborn screening are managed with conservative monitoring. Regular clinical assessment with attention to growth, development, and metabolic status is recommended. In many cases, no specific intervention is required.

evidence.snippet: All patients were regularly monitored once they were diagnosed, and each patient gradually had a normal diet after 6 months of age.
evidence.explanation: Describes gradual normalization of diet in monitored IBDD patients.

treatments/1.description: In the initial period after diagnosis, dietary management may include monitoring of protein intake. In the Chinese NBS cohort, patients gradually transitioned to a normal diet after 6 months of age with favorable outcomes.

evidence.snippet: Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is a defect in valine metabolism and was first reported in a child with cardiomyopathy, anemia, and secondary carnitine deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The index case had secondary carnitine deficiency, supporting supplementation when deficient.

evidence.snippet: Free carnitine was normal in all acylcarnitine samples.
evidence.explanation: Carnitine supplementation was not needed in this case as free carnitine remained normal.

treatments/2.description: Carnitine supplementation may be indicated in patients with documented secondary carnitine deficiency. The original symptomatic case with cardiomyopathy improved with oral L-carnitine. However, carnitine supplementation is not universally required when free carnitine levels are normal.

evidence.snippet: Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is a defect in valine metabolism and was first reported in a child with cardiomyopathy, anemia, and secondary carnitine deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The index case links the metabolic defect to secondary carnitine deficiency.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Carnitine supplementation is considered when metabolite shunting is accompanied by secondary carnitine depletion.

evidence.snippet: The patient was given, but has not used, a glucose polymer emergency regimen
evidence.explanation: Emergency regimen provided as precaution but never required in 10 years of follow-up.

treatments/3.description: A glucose polymer emergency regimen may be provided as a precautionary measure for managing potential hypoglycemic episodes during intercurrent illness, although its necessity in IBDD remains uncertain.

evidence.snippet: The concentration of C4-acylcarnitine in NBS plus subsequent genetic testing is necessary for IBDD diagnosis.
evidence.explanation: Confirms NBS combined with genetic testing as the diagnostic pathway.

treatments/4.description: IBDD is detectable through expanded newborn screening using tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) via elevated C4-acylcarnitine. A diagnostic follow-up algorithm involving plasma and urine acylcarnitine profiling, urinary organic acid analysis, and molecular genetic testing of ACAD8 has been developed for confirmatory diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that the new ratios are optimal indicators for identifying true positives, distinguishing between two rare diseases that share the same primary biomarker, improving the predictive positive value (PPV) and reducing the false positive rate
evidence.explanation: Novel ratios demonstrated statistical robustness for screening discrimination.

treatments/5.description: Novel C4-based acylcarnitine ratios have been proposed to reduce false positive rates in newborn screening and to improve discrimination between IBDD and SCADD. Seven ratios including C4/C0, C4/C5, C4/C6, and C4/C8 showed robust performance in distinguishing true positives from false positives.

evidence.snippet: Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (IBDD) is a rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder resulting from variants in ACAD8
evidence.explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance supports the role of genetic counseling.

evidence.snippet: In view of the limited experience worldwide, careful monitoring of the children is recommended.
evidence.explanation: Uncertainty about clinical significance supports counseling for informed family decision-making.

treatments/6.description: Genetic counseling is recommended for families of affected individuals, including discussion of autosomal recessive inheritance, the typically benign prognosis, recurrence risk, and the uncertain clinical significance of the condition.

evidence.snippet: the application of second-tier tests before the release of neonatal screening results reduced referrals by over 91.89% and improved the positive predictive value (PPV) for short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency/isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (SCADD/IBDD) screening.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that second-tier testing greatly reduces unnecessary referrals.

treatments/7.description: Second-tier testing using ultraperformance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to quantify ethylmalonate and isobutyrylglycine in dried blood spots can reduce referrals by over 90% while maintaining sensitivity for IBDD and SCADD differential diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: Our finding of mutated GLE1 exposes a common pathway connecting the genes implicated in LCCS1, LCCS2 and LCCS3 and elucidates mRNA processing as a critical molecular mechanism in motoneuron development and maturation.
evidence.explanation: Identifies mRNA processing as the molecular mechanism, and proposes it as the pathway shared across the anterior horn subtypes.

steps/12.description: GLE1 participates in nuclear mRNA export and translation. Human GLE1 variants cause LCCS1 with anterior-horn motor-neuron deficiency; zebrafish studies implicate dividing neural precursor survival and motor-axon arborization. The precise RNA targets and cell-autonomous contributions in affected human fetuses remain unresolved; a shared RNA pathway across LCCS1-3 remains a hypothesis.

evidence.snippet: an activator of the phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase/Akt pathway--regulating cell survival and vesicle trafficking
evidence.explanation: Names the pathway ERBB3 activates and the cellular functions it governs.

steps/13.description: The LCCS2 ERBB3 splice variant predicts loss of receptor signaling. The authors propose reduced PI3K/Akt survival signaling as a cause of neuronal apoptosis; Erbb3-null mice also lack Schwann-cell precursors. These are mechanistic hypotheses supporting, but not completing, the human genotype-to-neurogenic disease route.

evidence.snippet: Thus, a defect in the phosphatidylinositol pathway leading to a decrease in synthesis of PIP(2), a molecule active in endocytosis of synaptic vesicle proteins, culminates in lethal congenital arthrogryposis.
evidence.explanation: States the enzymatic deficiency, the downstream lipid, and its synaptic vesicle role in one sentence.

steps/14.description: The original PIP5K1C D253N allele markedly reduces recombinant PIPKI-gamma activity. The authors propose that reduced PIP2 impairs synaptic vesicle trafficking and neuronal function. Clinical similarity to LCCS2 does not demonstrate anterior-horn loss: the original LCCS3 families declined postmortem examination.

evidence.snippet: ADCY6 encodes a protein that belongs to the adenylate cyclase family responsible for the synthesis of cAMP.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the enzymatic function lost in the ADCY6 subtype.

steps/15.description: ADCY6 encodes an adenylate cyclase. Human peripheral amyelination and zebrafish knockdown support a myelination role, likely through cAMP. Complete absence of cAMP production or the full signaling sequence was not measured in affected humans.

evidence.snippet: Functional characterization of patient fibroblasts showed a significant reduction in cell proliferation and a delay in cell cycle progression.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived fibroblast assays establish cell-cycle abnormalities, not an in-vivo skeletal measurement.

evidence.snippet: Firstly, patient fibroblasts displayed a significant reduction in cilia number and length.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived fibroblasts show ciliary abnormalities supporting the proposed developmental mechanism.

steps/16.description: NEK9 p.Arg497* eliminates full-length protein in patient fibroblasts, with reduced proliferation, delayed cell-cycle progression, and fewer, shorter cilia. The authors propose a ciliopathy underlying the lethal skeletal dysplasia. The relative contributions of cell-cycle and ciliary dysfunction to fetal akinesia and skeletal growth are unresolved.

evidence.snippet: We now show that a recessive mutation abrogating all functional domains in the same gene leads to LCCS.
evidence.explanation: Establishes recessive MYBPC1 loss of function as the LCCS4 mechanism.

steps/17.description: Recessive MYBPC1 truncation abrogates functional protein domains. A muscle contractile route is supported by the protein role and human causal genotype, but the precise fetal muscle structural defect is not demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: Genotype-phenotype correlation in these patients and previously published cases with respective variants resulted in the definition of a DST-associated lethal congenital contracture syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Establishes DST as the gene defining a lethal congenital contracture syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Variants that also impact DST-a besides DST-b result in a more severe, lethal congenital contracture syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Gives the isoform-dependent severity relationship that separates the lethal phenotype from the congenital myopathy.

steps/18.description: Biallelic DST variants affecting both DST-a and DST-b cause a lethal arthrogryposis presentation. The relative neuronal and muscle contributions are unresolved; functional and biopsy findings from DST-b-only myopathy cannot be assigned wholesale to this combined-isoform disorder.

evidence.snippet: The most severe forms of motoneuron disease manifest in utero are characterized by marked atrophy of spinal cord motoneurons and fetal immobility.
evidence.explanation: Frames LCCS1 as an in utero motor neuron disease with spinal motoneuron atrophy and consequent immobility.

evidence.snippet: Lethal congenital contractural syndrome type 2 (LCCS2) is an autosomal recessive neurogenic form of arthrogryposis that is associated with atrophy of the anterior horn of the spinal cord.
evidence.explanation: Records anterior horn atrophy as the neuropathological lesion in LCCS2 as well, extending the node beyond LCCS1.

evidence.snippet: Unexpectedly, the motoneuron deficiency results from apoptosis of neural precursors, not of differentiated motoneurons.
evidence.explanation: Refines the cellular mechanism: the motoneuron loss is a precursor survival defect rather than degeneration of mature neurons.

steps/19.description: Anterior-horn motor-neuron deficiency or atrophy is documented in GLE1 and ERBB3 disease. Zebrafish Gle1 studies identify apoptosis of dividing neural precursors rather than differentiated motor neurons. This cellular route must not be generalized to PIP5K1C disease, whose original series lacked autopsies.

evidence.snippet: Morpholino knockdown of the zebrafish orthologs led to severe and specific defects in peripheral myelin in spite of the presence of Schwann cells.
evidence.explanation: Shows the ADCY6 lesion is a myelination failure rather than an absence of Schwann cells.

evidence.snippet: We have shown that the peripheral nerves in affected individuals from one family lack myelin basic protein, suggesting that this disease in affected individuals is due to defective myelination of the peripheral axons during fetal development.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates absent peripheral myelin in ADGRG6/GPR126-related disease in human tissue.

steps/20.description: Peripheral myelination is deficient in ADCY6- and ADGRG6-associated disease. Human nerve pathology supports this lesion; ADCY6 knockdown and ADGRG6 studies in fish and mice inform the proposed signaling routes. Schwann precursor loss in Erbb3-null mice is a different model observation and is not asserted as measured human LCCS2 myelin pathology.

evidence.snippet: The axoglial contact between gliomedin and NF186 is essential for the initial clustering of Na+ channels at developing nodes.
evidence.explanation: The source summarizes the molecular requirement for gliomedin/NF186 contact during initial sodium-channel clustering; this background statement is distinct from its human microscopy and variant assays.

evidence.snippet: These data indicate that mutations of GLDN or CNTNAP1 (MIM: 616286), encoding essential components of the nodes of Ranvier and paranodes, respectively, lead to inherited nodopathies, a distinct disease entity among peripheral neuropathies.
evidence.explanation: The authors place GLDN nodal and CNTNAP1 paranodal defects in the broader inherited-nodopathy category while explicitly distinguishing their anatomical sites. This node represents the GLDN nodal lesion; CNTNAP1 is modeled separately.

steps/21.description: GLDN encodes gliomedin, which contributes to nodal sodium-channel clustering through axonal ligands including NF186. Human nodal abnormalities and variant assays support a nodopathy. GLDN-null mice can retain conduction and lack arthrogryposis, so complete conduction abolition cannot be inferred from loss of gliomedin alone.

evidence.snippet: Knockdown experiments of zbtb42 in zebrafish consistently resulted in grossly abnormal skeletal muscle development and myofibrillar disorganization at the microscopic level.
evidence.explanation: Shows the ZBTB42 lesion is a muscle developmental and myofibrillar defect.

steps/22.description: ZBTB42 knockdown causes myofibrillar disorganization and abnormal neuromuscular junctions in zebrafish, with impaired coiling and escape movement. Wild-type human ZBTB42, but not the variant construct, rescues the model phenotype. Human muscle biopsy and autopsy were declined, so the exact human tissue lesion remains inferred.

evidence.snippet: In vitro membrane tubulation, trafficking and GTPase assays are consistent with an impact of the DNM2p.Phe379Val mutation on endocytosis.
evidence.explanation: Functional assays localizing the DNM2 lesion to endocytosis.

evidence.snippet: knockdown approaches in zebrafish resulting in defects in muscle organization and angiogenesis support a pleiotropic role for DNM2 during fetal development in vertebrates and humans
evidence.explanation: Supports the pleiotropic muscle-and-vascular role that separates this node from the purely myofibrillar one.

steps/23.description: The DNM2 p.Phe379Val allele impairs endocytosis in assays and is associated with a severe recessive congenital syndrome. Zebrafish knockdown affects muscle organization and angiogenesis. The authors propose altered developmental endocytosis as an explanation for pleiotropic clinical manifestations, without establishing the specific human tissue route to each finding.

evidence.snippet: These 2 families illustrate severe progressive peripheral demyelinating neuropathy due to the absence of septate paranodal junctions and central hypomyelination with neurodegeneration in CNTNAP1-associated arthrogryposis multiplex congenita.
evidence.explanation: The authors explicitly attribute progressive peripheral neuropathy to missing paranodal junctions and document associated central disease.

steps/24.description: CNTNAP1/CASPR1 deficiency disrupts septate paranodal junctions in peripheral nerves and is proposed to disturb glial-axonal interactions centrally. This is anatomically distinct from gliomedin-dependent nodal assembly.

evidence.snippet: Patients showed a marked reduction in motor nerve conduction velocity (<10 m/s)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the conduction failure in affected individuals.

steps/25.description: Peripheral motor signaling is impaired in CNTNAP1 and some GLDN cases. Original CNTNAP1 families had motor velocities below 10 m/s, but this threshold is not universal, and a GLDN child had normal repeat studies at seven months. The functional route to weakness and reduced movement is supported indirectly by the human neuropathy and nodal-pathology context.

evidence.snippet: Neuropathologic examination revealed anterior horn cell loss and lateral corticospinal tract degeneration in spinal cord, with marked muscular atrophy.
evidence.explanation: This ungenotyped fetal akinesia case provides supporting neurogenic pathological context, not direct proof of a numbered LCCS genotype.

steps/26.description: Loss of effective developing motor innervation can impair muscle growth and contraction. GLE1 fetal autopsies show severely hypoplastic musculature together with anterior-horn deficiency. The causal interpretation is supported indirectly by fetal neurogenic pathology; PIP5K1C muscle wasting is not assigned to this specific lesion without autopsy evidence.

evidence.snippet: Insufficient swallowing aggravated by paresis of both the right vocal cord and right side of the soft palate prompted gastrostomy tube placement at 4 months of age.
evidence.explanation: Documents insufficient swallowing and the gastrostomy it required in a surviving LCCS11 child.

steps/27.description: Right vocal-cord and right soft-palate paresis aggravated swallowing insufficiency in a GLDN survivor. The report establishes this functional contribution without identifying the upstream cranial motor lesion.

evidence.snippet: Thirty-nine cases had lethal congenital contracture syndrome (LCCS) clinically characterized by total immobility of the fetus at all ultrasound examinations (12 weeks or later)
evidence.explanation: Establishes total fetal immobility from 12 weeks as a defining clinical feature of LCCS in a population-based series.

steps/28.description: Reduced or absent prenatal movement across the LCCS spectrum. Total immobility at every ultrasound examination from 12 weeks or later characterized all 39 clinically defined Finnish LCCS cases; the frequency band refers to that series, not all genotypes or all gestational examinations. Reduced movement is a shared functional consequence of distinct motor-unit disorders and can also accompany NEK9 skeletal dysplasia. It can cause a fetal deformation sequence without explaining every primary skeletal, cerebral, vascular or visceral manifestation.

evidence.snippet: The common feature of this sequence is decreased fetal activity, which leads to a failure of normal deglutition, resulting in polyhydramnios.
evidence.explanation: The source explicitly gives the fetal activity-to-deglutition-to-amniotic-fluid sequence.

steps/29.description: Impaired fetal deglutition reduces amniotic-fluid clearance. This prenatal mechanism is distinguished from postnatal swallowing insufficiency with documented focal bulbar paresis in a GLDN survivor.

evidence.snippet: multiple joint contractures in both upper and lower limbs, hydrops, and fetal death before the 32nd week of pregnancy
evidence.explanation: Records the contracture distribution in the LCCS cases.

steps/30.description: Congenital contractures involving multiple upper- and lower-limb joints. The frequency band reflects the defining finding in the 39 Finnish LCCS cases. Joint distribution varies between families and subtypes; contractures can improve with therapy in surviving GLDN-associated disease.

evidence.snippet: To our knowledge, among the herein 28 reviewed cases, 16 reported respiratory findings, pulmonary hypoplasia being the most frequent (75%, 12/16), followed by pulmonary insufficiency or need of respiratory support.
evidence.explanation: The 75% proportion is 12/16 respiratory-described cases, not 12/28 or an umbrella prevalence estimate.

steps/31.description: Underdeveloped lungs documented in several subtypes. A GLDN literature review found pulmonary hypoplasia in 12 of 16 cases with reported respiratory findings among 28 total cases; this selected reporting denominator cannot estimate prevalence across all GLDN cases or the LCCS umbrella. Deficient fetal respiratory-muscle movement can impair lung development; thoracic dysplasia is an additional potential contributor in NEK9 disease. Lung underdevelopment can cause respiratory insufficiency but does not account for all respiratory impairment in survivors.

evidence.snippet: The fetus exhibited hydrops, short long bones, fixed limb joints, absent fetal movements, and polyhydramnios.
evidence.explanation: Records polyhydramnios in an LCCS11 fetus.

steps/32.description: Excess amniotic fluid occurs in several subtypes and may follow impaired fetal deglutition. A reported GLDN-associated fetus had polyhydramnios with akinesia and hydrops; the report included one GLDN variant of uncertain significance and provides no umbrella frequency.

evidence.snippet: accompanied by hydrops, micrognatia, pulmonary hypoplasia, pterygia and multiple joint contractures
evidence.explanation: Lists micrognathia among the characteristic LCCS1 features. The source spells it "micrognatia"; the quote preserves the source spelling.

evidence.snippet: At 25 weeks of pregnancy, MRI revealed micrognathia and fixed extension of the arms and flexion of the elbows, wrists, and hands
evidence.explanation: Full text of the same study indexed as PMID:26004201 documents micrognathia in the ADGRG6 Family 2 fetus; this is not independent replication.

steps/33.description: Small mandible described in classic GLE1-related LCCS1 and in ADGRG6-associated fetuses. This anatomical size finding is distinct from the retruded jaw position described as retrognathia in a GLDN-associated fetus.

evidence.snippet: postmortem studies confirmed the prenatal findings: distal arthrogryposis, fetal growth restriction, pulmonary hypoplasia, and retrognathia
evidence.explanation: Postmortem confirmation of fetal growth restriction in LCCS11.

steps/34.description: Growth restriction is reported in some LCCS pregnancies. The cited GLDN-associated fetus had estimated weight at the fourth percentile and absent umbilical-artery end-diastolic flow; placental or vascular contributions cannot be separated from the fetal disorder. Other GLDN cases had normal birth-weight percentiles.

evidence.snippet: severe muscle wasting and atrophy, mainly in the legs
evidence.explanation: The original PIP5K1C neonates had muscle wasting; the families declined autopsy, so an anterior-horn cause is not demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: His neurologic examination was notable for myopathic facies, very weak to absent deep tendon reflexes, and symmetric atrophy and weakness of his proximal muscles.
evidence.explanation: The surviving GLDN-related child had proximal atrophy and weakness on examination, rather than a universal congenital muscle-hypoplasia phenotype.

steps/35.description: Loss of muscle bulk is reported in PIP5K1C-associated neonates and GLDN survivors, with different possible neurogenic or muscular contributions. This is distinguished from the severely hypoplastic musculature documented at GLE1 fetal autopsy.

evidence.snippet: Lethal congenital contracture syndrome 1 (LCCS1, MIM 253310) is an autosomal recessive condition characterized by total immobility of the fetus, detectable at the 13th week of pregnancy, accompanied by hydrops, micrognatia, pulmonary hypoplasia, pterygia and multiple joint contractures
evidence.explanation: Lists pterygia among the characteristic features of LCCS1 specifically, which is the subtype this phenotype is tagged to.

evidence.snippet: Fetopathological examination of the aborted fetus confirmed that the joint retractions were associated with pterygium of the right elbow and axilla
evidence.explanation: Full text of PMID:26004201 documents the anatomical webbing in Family 1.

steps/36.description: Webbing across joints is reported in classic GLE1 disease and in an ADGRG6-associated fetus. It was explicitly absent in the original ERBB3 and PIP5K1C kindreds.

evidence.snippet: in three consanguineous patients with a lethal congenital syndrome associating akinesia, joint contractures, hypotonia, skeletal abnormalities, and brain and retinal hemorrhages
evidence.explanation: Reports the intracranial haemorrhage that helps define the DNM2 subtype.

evidence.snippet: In addition, they showed retinal hemorrhages, whereas MRI analysis revealed symmetric subdural hematomas for AFB3 and blood in the subarachnoid cavity for AFB4
evidence.explanation: Full text of the same study indexed as PMID:23092955 distinguishes retinal hemorrhage in the three siblings from intracranial bleeding described in AFB3 and AFB4; this is not independent replication.

steps/37.description: Brain hemorrhage was present in two of the three homozygous DNM2 p.Phe379Val siblings (AFB3 and AFB4); AFB2 had a normal brain MRI. The frequency band applies only to this three-sibling series.

evidence.snippet: in three consanguineous patients with a lethal congenital syndrome associating akinesia, joint contractures, hypotonia, skeletal abnormalities, and brain and retinal hemorrhages
evidence.explanation: Reports retinal haemorrhage in the DNM2-mutated patients.

evidence.snippet: In addition, they showed retinal hemorrhages, whereas MRI analysis revealed symmetric subdural hematomas for AFB3 and blood in the subarachnoid cavity for AFB4
evidence.explanation: Full text of the same study indexed as PMID:23092955 distinguishes retinal hemorrhage in the three siblings from intracranial bleeding described in AFB3 and AFB4; this is not independent replication.

steps/38.description: Retinal hemorrhage was documented in all three homozygous DNM2 p.Phe379Val siblings, including the sibling without intracranial hemorrhage. The frequency band applies to this family only, not all DNM2 alleles or LCCS.

evidence.snippet: We described the features of multiple joint contractures in our fetuses, including bilateral talipes equinovarus, stiffness in the limbs, extended knees, persistently closed hands and overlapping fingers
evidence.explanation: Documents bilateral talipes equinovarus as part of the contracture pattern in LCCS3 fetuses.

steps/39.description: Equinovarus clubfoot is documented bilaterally in the PIP5K1C fetal pedigree. The GLDN fetus described as left pes equinus does not independently support a varus component and is not used for this binding.

evidence.snippet: His neurologic examination was notable for myopathic facies, very weak to absent deep tendon reflexes, and symmetric atrophy and weakness of his proximal muscles.
evidence.explanation: Documents absent deep tendon reflexes on examination in a GLDN-mutated child.

evidence.snippet: The three patients displayed no reflexes and suffered from severe hypotonia and respiratory insufficiency from birth, while they exhibited contractures of several joints and skeletal abnormalities with thin ribs and bones
evidence.explanation: The same DNM2 study explicitly records absent reflexes in all three affected siblings; this observation is distinct from the very weak-to-absent reflex description in GLDN disease.

steps/40.description: Absent tendon reflexes are documented in GLDN-associated disease and in the DNM2 sibling series. Weak but present reflexes are broader than areflexia; the finding alone cannot distinguish a peripheral nerve lesion from severe muscle disease.

evidence.snippet: Insufficient swallowing aggravated by paresis of both the right vocal cord and right side of the soft palate prompted gastrostomy tube placement at 4 months of age.
evidence.explanation: Documents insufficient swallowing and the gastrostomy it required in a surviving LCCS11 child.

steps/41.description: Postnatal swallowing insufficiency in a GLDN survivor was aggravated by right vocal-cord and right soft-palate paresis and required gastrostomy at four months. Most feeding was oral by 28 months. This does not establish that all postnatal dysphagia is persistence of impaired fetal swallowing.

evidence.snippet: including bilateral talipes equinovarus, stiffness in the limbs, extended knees, persistently closed hands and overlapping fingers
evidence.explanation: Documents the closed-hand and overlapping-finger posture in LCCS3 fetuses.

steps/42.description: Overlapping flexed fingers were reported in the PIP5K1C fetal pedigree. Hand clenching and fixed knee posture in the same report are separate findings rather than synonyms for finger overlap.

evidence.snippet: a lethal congenital syndrome associating akinesia, joint contractures, hypotonia, skeletal abnormalities, and brain and retinal hemorrhages
evidence.explanation: Lists hypotonia among the presenting features.

evidence.snippet: The three patients displayed no reflexes and suffered from severe hypotonia and respiratory insufficiency from birth, while they exhibited contractures of several joints and skeletal abnormalities with thin ribs and bones
evidence.explanation: The full clinical narrative confirms severe hypotonia in all three DNM2 siblings; Table 1 specifies generalized severe hypotonia. This is the same study as PMID:23092955.

steps/43.description: Generalized severe hypotonia was recorded in all three homozygous DNM2 p.Phe379Val siblings. The molecular-to-tone pathway may involve muscle and peripheral nerve dysfunction and is not reconstructed by the human clinical observations alone.

evidence.snippet: Neuropathological analysis shows lack of anterior horn motoneurons, severe atrophy of the ventral spinal cord and hypoplastic, nearly absent skeletal muscles
evidence.explanation: The GLE1 autopsy phenotype specifically supports muscle hypoplasia.

steps/44.description: Severely hypoplastic, nearly absent skeletal muscles were found at GLE1-associated fetal autopsy; this is a developmental reduction in muscle tissue rather than evidence of acquired atrophy.

evidence.snippet: We described the features of multiple joint contractures in our fetuses, including bilateral talipes equinovarus, stiffness in the limbs, extended knees, persistently closed hands and overlapping fingers
evidence.explanation: Supports the persistently closed-hand posture in this fetal pedigree, without making a population-frequency claim.

steps/45.description: Persistently closed hands were reported in the PIP5K1C fetal pedigree, distinct from the overlapping-finger description in another examined fetus.

evidence.snippet: We described the features of multiple joint contractures in our fetuses, including bilateral talipes equinovarus, stiffness in the limbs, extended knees, persistently closed hands and overlapping fingers
evidence.explanation: The fixed limb-contracture context supports extended-knee contractures rather than an isolated positional observation.

steps/46.description: Fixed extended knees were reported in the PIP5K1C fetal pedigree and the ZBTB42 index case. This differs from the flexion contractures described in other families.

evidence.snippet: Due to persistent respiratory insufficiency associated with pulmonary hypoplasia and diaphragm paralysis, he underwent tracheostomy at 3 months of age.
evidence.explanation: Documents diaphragm paralysis and its respiratory context in the Family 2 child.

steps/47.description: Diaphragm paralysis accompanied pulmonary hypoplasia and persistent respiratory insufficiency in one GLDN survivor. Diaphragm paralysis contributed alongside hypoplastic lungs to the respiratory insufficiency; its upstream neural or muscular cause was not localized.

evidence.snippet: Then, she underwent vaginal delivery prematurely at 26 weeks, and the baby passed away after birth due to respiratory failure.
